name: comp-168

frames.best_why: Nine is chosen in white while the hovered ten shows its outline, with both end labels in view.

tagline: A 0 to 10 strip of boxes asking how likely you would recommend.
summary: Eleven joined cells from 0 to 10 under the question How likely are you to recommend us?, with an angry face and Not likely at one end and Very likely with a heart-eyes face at the other. Clicking a cell keeps it lit white.
appearance: A white question sits above an unbroken row of eleven square cells numbered 0 to 10, each with a thin grey border and the outer ends rounded, on black. A small angry face and Not likely sit under the left end, Very likely and a grinning face under the right.
behaviour: Nothing is chosen at first. Hovering a cell tints it grey, and clicking fills it white with dark digits; the recording steps from 6 to 9 to 10.
demo_content: How likely are you to recommend us?; cells 0 through 10; Not likely and Very likely end labels
search_phrases: how likely are you to recommend us
rate us from zero to ten
use_when: Running a one-question recommendation survey where the familiar 0 to 10 score is expected.
avoid_when: Eleven cells need horizontal room, so on a narrow phone the outer boxes crowd their digits.
customise: The 0 to 10 values, the question and the two end labels are written in the file; shorten the array to change the range. Cell height, radius and the filled colour are classes in the same file.
weight_why: Eleven plain cells over native radios with a short colour and border fade.

a11y.note: Radios take arrow keys and show a focus ring, and the legend frames the question, but each option is named only by its digit.

issues: Nothing is selected at the start, so the strip looks unanswered with no cue to choose.
The outer cells are narrow, leaving their digits close to the borders.
polish_why: Even joined cells and a clear chosen fill; plain styling and cramped end cells.
